entries.title: Heart Failure (CHF)
entries.contentDescription: The heart can't pump enough blood to meet the body's metabolic demands — leading to congestion (backward failure) and/or poor perfusion (forward failure).

entries.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome / MI
entries.contentDescription: A spectrum of myocardial ischemia from unstable angina → NSTEMI → STEMI, caused by acute coronary artery plaque rupture and thrombus.

entries.title: Atrial Fibrillation
entries.contentDescription: A supraventricular tachyarrhythmia with disorganized atrial activity — 'irregularly irregular' rhythm — that risks thromboembolic stroke and rate-related heart failure.

entries.title: Hypertension
entries.contentDescription: Chronically elevated arterial pressure — the 'silent killer' — driving stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, and retinopathy over time.

entries.title: Aortic Stenosis (Valvular Disease)
entries.contentDescription: Progressive narrowing of the aortic valve creates a fixed obstruction to left ventricular outflow — the heart pumps harder against a closing door until symptoms signal danger.

entries.title: COPD
entries.contentDescription: Chronic, progressive airflow limitation from chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema — largely caused by smoking — punctuated by acute exacerbations.

entries.title: Asthma
entries.contentDescription: Chronic airway inflammation with reversible bronchoconstriction and hyperresponsiveness — episodic wheeze, cough, and dyspnea triggered by allergens, exercise, cold, or infection.

entries.title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
entries.contentDescription: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma acquired outside healthcare settings — fever, productive cough, dyspnea, and a new infiltrate on imaging.

entries.title: Pulmonary Embolism
entries.contentDescription: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries — usually by a clot embolized from a deep vein — causing sudden dyspnea, hypoxia, and potential hemodynamic collapse.

entries.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
entries.contentDescription: A life-threatening hyperglycemic emergency of insulin deficiency — hyperglycemia, ketosis, and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis — most common in type 1 diabetes.

entries.title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
entries.contentDescription: A chronic disorder of insulin resistance and progressive β-cell dysfunction causing hyperglycemia, with long-term micro- and macrovascular complications.

entries.title: Metabolic Syndrome
entries.contentDescription: A cluster of five cardiometabolic risk factors — central adiposity, atherogenic dyslipidemia, elevated blood pressure, and dysglycemia — that together multiply the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

entries.title: Hypothyroidism
entries.contentDescription: Deficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism system-wide — fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, and bradycardia — with myxedema coma at the severe extreme.

entries.title: Thyroid Storm / Hyperthyroidism
entries.contentDescription: Excess thyroid hormone accelerates metabolism — weight loss, heat intolerance, palpitations — with thyroid storm as the life-threatening decompensated extreme.

entries.title: Infective Endocarditis
entries.contentDescription: A microbial infection of the endocardial surface — usually valves — that turns platelet-fibrin vegetations into embolizing, valve-destroying vegetations.

entries.title: Acute Pericarditis
entries.contentDescription: Inflammation of the pericardial sac — classically pleuritic, positional chest pain that improves sitting forward with a pathognomonic friction rub.

entries.title: Cardiomyopathy
entries.contentDescription: A disease of the heart muscle itself — impairing the ability to pump or fill, independent of coronary, valvular, or hypertensive disease.

entries.title: Peripheral Arterial Disease
entries.contentDescription: Atherosclerotic narrowing of the limb arteries — the same plaque as coronary disease, just in the legs, and a powerful marker of systemic cardiovascular risk.

entries.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis
entries.contentDescription: A blood clot in a deep vein — usually the leg — that threatens the limb locally and the lungs if it embolizes.

entries.title: Aortic Aneurysm & Dissection
entries.contentDescription: A weakened or torn aorta — the vessel either balloons silently (aneurysm) or splits along its wall (dissection), and both can rupture into sudden death.

entries.title: Cardiac Arrest (ACLS)
entries.contentDescription: Sudden cessation of effective cardiac output — survival hinges on early high-quality CPR and early defibrillation, not the drugs.

entries.title: Hyperlipidemia
entries.contentDescription: Excess circulating lipids that silently drive atherosclerosis — the modifiable engine behind most heart attacks and strokes.

entries.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
entries.contentDescription: Diffuse inflammatory alveolar injury causing non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxemia — stiff, wet, leaky lungs that resist oxygen no matter how hard you push.

entries.title: Pneumothorax
entries.contentDescription: Air in the pleural space collapses the lung — ranging from a small spontaneous leak to life-threatening tension physiology.

entries.title: Tuberculosis
entries.contentDescription: A chronic granulomatous infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis — the world's leading infectious killer, spread by airborne droplet nuclei and controlled by prolonged multidrug therapy.

entries.title: Lung Cancer
entries.contentDescription: The #1 cause of cancer death in both sexes — a smoking-driven malignancy split into NSCLC and aggressive SCLC, where molecular profiling now dictates therapy.

entries.title: Pleural Effusion
entries.contentDescription: Abnormal fluid in the pleural space — the lung's problem is often the heart's, the kidney's, or the malignancy's fault.

entries.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
entries.contentDescription: Repetitive upper-airway collapse during sleep causing intermittent hypoxia and fragmented sleep — the treatable driver of hypertension, arrhythmia, and daytime somnolence.

entries.title: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS)
entries.contentDescription: Profound hyperglycemia with severe dehydration and hyperosmolarity but little-to-no ketosis — the slow, deadly cousin of DKA in type 2 diabetes.

entries.title: Hypoglycemia
entries.contentDescription: A dangerous drop in plasma glucose that starves the brain — the fastest-reversible cause of altered mental status you must never miss.

entries.title: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
entries.contentDescription: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells produces absolute insulin deficiency — lifelong exogenous insulin is non-negotiable and its omission risks DKA.

entries.title: Cushing's Syndrome
entries.contentDescription: A state of chronic glucocorticoid excess — whether from steroids, a pituitary tumor, or an adrenal source — that reshapes the body's metabolism, immunity, and appearance.

entries.title: Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison's)
entries.contentDescription: The adrenal glands fail to make enough cortisol (and often aldosterone) — leaving the body unable to mount a stress response and prone to fatal shock.

entries.title: SIADH
entries.contentDescription: Too much ADH holds onto water — diluting the blood into a euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia.

entries.title: Diabetes Insipidus
entries.contentDescription: A disorder of water balance — the body cannot concentrate urine, producing large volumes of dilute urine and driving relentless thirst.

entries.title: GERD
entries.contentDescription: Retrograde flow of gastric contents into the esophagus from a failing lower esophageal sphincter — common, chronic, and occasionally a gateway to Barrett's esophagus.

entries.title: Hyperparathyroidism
entries.contentDescription: Excess parathyroid hormone drives calcium out of bone and into blood — "stones, bones, groans, and psychiatric moans."

entries.title: Peptic Ulcer Disease
entries.contentDescription: A break in the gastric or duodenal mucosa driven by an imbalance between acid-peptic aggression and mucosal defense — most often from H. pylori or NSAIDs.

entries.title: Upper GI Bleed
entries.contentDescription: Bleeding proximal to the ligament of Treitz — a potentially life-threatening emergency where resuscitation comes before diagnosis.

entries.title: Acute Pancreatitis
entries.contentDescription: Autodigestion of the pancreas by prematurely activated enzymes — a self-inflicted chemical burn that ranges from mild edema to lethal necrosis.

entries.title: Cirrhosis
entries.contentDescription: Irreversible hepatic fibrosis with nodular regeneration — the liver's final common pathway to failure and portal hypertension.

entries.title: Cholecystitis & Cholelithiasis
entries.contentDescription: A gallstone lodged in the cystic duct turns a fatty meal into a gangrene threat — obstruction breeds inflammation, and inflammation breeds emergency.

entries.title: Viral Hepatitis
entries.contentDescription: Virus-driven liver inflammation — ranging from a self-limited flu-like illness to fulminant failure or decades-later cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

entries.title: Appendicitis
entries.contentDescription: Obstruction of the appendiceal lumen triggers a cascade of distension, ischemia, and infection — the most common surgical emergency of the abdomen.

entries.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
entries.contentDescription: Chronic immune-mediated bowel inflammation with two faces — ulcerative colitis (continuous, mucosal, colon-only) and Crohn's disease (skip lesions, transmural, mouth-to-anus).

entries.title: Diverticulitis
entries.contentDescription: Inflammation or micro-perforation of colonic diverticula — the "left lower quadrant appendicitis" of older adults.

entries.title: Bowel Obstruction
entries.contentDescription: Mechanical or functional blockage of intestinal flow — a plumbing problem that becomes a perfusion emergency when the bowel strangulates.

entries.title: C. difficile Colitis
entries.contentDescription: Antibiotic-triggered overgrowth of a toxin-producing spore-former — the classic cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea.

entries.title: Acute Kidney Injury
entries.contentDescription: An abrupt decline in kidney function over hours to days — retained nitrogenous waste, dysregulated fluids, electrolytes, and acid-base balance.

entries.title: Urinary Tract Infection
entries.contentDescription: Bacterial colonization of the urinary tract — ranging from simple cystitis to life-threatening pyelonephritis and urosepsis.

entries.title: Chronic Kidney Disease
entries.contentDescription: Progressive, irreversible loss of nephron function over months to years — silent until late, and best measured by eGFR plus albuminuria.

entries.title: Nephrolithiasis (Kidney Stones)
entries.contentDescription: Crystals precipitate in supersaturated urine and lodge in the ureter — producing the sudden, writhing, colicky flank pain that no position relieves.

entries.title: Hyperkalemia
entries.contentDescription: A serum potassium above the normal range — dangerous because it destabilizes cardiac membranes long before symptoms appear.

entries.title: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
entries.contentDescription: Age-related, DHT-driven proliferation of the prostatic transition zone that squeezes the urethra — producing bothersome lower urinary tract symptoms, not cancer.

entries.title: Hyponatremia
entries.contentDescription: Serum sodium <135 mEq/L reflecting a relative excess of water — not a lack of salt — driven mostly by inappropriate ADH activity.

entries.title: Ischemic Stroke
entries.contentDescription: Sudden focal neurologic deficit from arterial occlusion — time is brain, and every minute untreated loses ~1.9 million neurons.

entries.title: Transient Ischemic Attack
entries.contentDescription: A transient neurologic deficit from focal brain, spinal cord, or retinal ischemia without acute infarction — a warning shot for impending stroke, not a "mini-stroke" to shrug off.

entries.title: Bacterial Meningitis
entries.contentDescription: A neurologic emergency where pyogenic infection of the leptomeninges triggers inflammation of the CSF and brain — every hour of delayed antibiotics raises mortality.

entries.title: Seizure & Status Epilepticus
entries.contentDescription: Hypersynchronous cortical discharge — a self-limited event that becomes a time-is-brain emergency once it fails to stop on its own.

entries.title: Parkinson's Disease
entries.contentDescription: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder of dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra — producing the classic tetrad of tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability.

entries.title: Alzheimer's & Dementia
entries.contentDescription: A progressive, acquired decline in memory and cognition severe enough to impair daily function — Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause, driven by amyloid-β plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles.

entries.title: Multiple Sclerosis
entries.contentDescription: A chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the CNS — lesions disseminated in space and time that strip myelin from brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves.

entries.title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
entries.contentDescription: An acute, immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy causing rapidly ascending weakness and areflexia — a neurologic emergency because of respiratory and autonomic failure.

entries.title: Myasthenia Gravis
entries.contentDescription: An autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction — producing fatigable, fluctuating weakness that worsens with use and improves with rest.

entries.title: Increased Intracranial Pressure / TBI
entries.contentDescription: A fixed skull with rising volume — every added milliliter of blood, brain, or CSF steals perfusion until the brain herniates.

entries.title: Spinal Cord Injury
entries.contentDescription: A disruption of ascending and descending cord tracts — where preserving perfusion and preventing secondary injury matters as much as the initial impact.

entries.title: Migraine & Headache
entries.contentDescription: A recurrent primary headache driven by neurovascular dysfunction and cortical spreading depression — the art is separating benign primary headache from the deadly secondary mimic.

entries.title: Iron Deficiency Anemia
entries.contentDescription: The most common anemia worldwide — a microcytic, hypochromic anemia driven by depleted iron stores that starves hemoglobin synthesis.

entries.title: B12 / Folate Deficiency Anemia
entries.contentDescription: Impaired DNA synthesis from vitamin deficiency yields large, immature red cells — a macrocytic megaloblastic anemia where B12 loss uniquely threatens the nervous system.

entries.title: Sickle Cell Disease
entries.contentDescription: A single amino-acid swap turns hemoglobin into a polymerizing sludge — chronic hemolysis punctuated by agonizing vaso-occlusive crises.

entries.title: Leukemia
entries.contentDescription: Malignant clonal proliferation of white-cell precursors that crowds out normal marrow — producing anemia, bleeding, and infection while flooding the blood with abnormal leukocytes.

entries.title: Lymphoma
entries.contentDescription: A malignancy of lymphocytes arising in lymph nodes and lymphoid tissue — split fundamentally into Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, which differ profoundly in behavior, spread, and prognosis.

entries.title: Thrombocytopenia
entries.contentDescription: A platelet count <150,000/µL from decreased production, increased destruction, or sequestration — bleeding risk climbs sharply once counts fall below <20,000/µL.

entries.title: Sepsis & Septic Shock
entries.contentDescription: A dysregulated host response to infection causing life-threatening organ dysfunction — sepsis becomes septic shock when circulatory and metabolic derangement persists despite adequate fluid resuscitation.

entries.title: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
entries.contentDescription: A systemic disorder of unbridled coagulation and consumption — the body clots everywhere and bleeds everywhere at the same time.

entries.title: Cellulitis
entries.contentDescription: An acute bacterial infection of the deep dermis and subcutaneous fat — spreading, ill-defined redness that is warm, tender, and swollen.

entries.title: HIV / AIDS
entries.contentDescription: A retrovirus that hijacks and depletes CD4 T-cells — untreated it erodes immunity until opportunistic infections define AIDS, but modern ART makes it a manageable chronic disease.

entries.title: Influenza
entries.contentDescription: An acute respiratory illness caused by orthomyxoviruses — abrupt fever, myalgia, and cough that spreads in seasonal epidemics and can turn deadly through pneumonia.

entries.title: COVID-19
entries.contentDescription: A SARS-CoV-2 respiratory infection spanning asymptomatic carriage to hypoxemic respiratory failure — where early antivirals and oxygen-guided steroids drive outcomes.

entries.title: Osteomyelitis
entries.contentDescription: Infection of bone — where microbes seed the marrow and cortex, triggering inflammation, ischemia, and progressive bony destruction.

entries.title: Fractures
entries.contentDescription: A break in bony continuity — where mechanical force exceeds bone strength, threatening not just the bone but the neurovascular structures around it.

entries.title: Hip Fracture
entries.contentDescription: A proximal femur fracture — usually a low-energy fall in an older adult with weak bone, where the fracture is the visible half of the problem and the frailty behind it is the other.

entries.title: Osteoporosis
entries.contentDescription: A silent skeletal thief — bone microarchitecture deteriorates until a low-trauma fracture announces the disease.

entries.title: Osteoarthritis
entries.contentDescription: The "wear-and-tear" arthritis of aging — but really an active metabolically-driven joint failure with cartilage breakdown, subchondral bone remodeling, and low-grade inflammation.

entries.title: Low Back Pain
entries.contentDescription: The most common musculoskeletal complaint in medicine — where the diagnosis is usually nonspecific, most of the skill is in excluding the few dangerous causes, and imaging early makes outcomes worse rather than better.

entries.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis
entries.contentDescription: A chronic, symmetric, autoimmune polyarthritis that erodes synovial joints — early DMARD therapy is the key to preventing irreversible destruction.

entries.title: Gout
entries.contentDescription: A crystal-induced inflammatory arthritis driven by monosodium urate deposition — the most common inflammatory arthritis in men, and it is fully preventable with urate-lowering therapy.

entries.title: Compartment Syndrome
entries.contentDescription: A surgical emergency where rising pressure within a closed fascial compartment strangles its own blood supply — muscle and nerve die within hours unless the fascia is released.

entries.title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
entries.contentDescription: A chronic autoimmune disease of immune-complex deposition that can attack nearly any organ — the great multisystem "mimicker" driven by loss of self-tolerance.

entries.title: Major Depressive Disorder
entries.contentDescription: A pervasive disorder of mood, cognition, and neurovegetative function — where at least 2 weeks of depressed mood or anhedonia hijacks a person's biology, thoughts, and will to live.

entries.title: Anxiety Disorders
entries.contentDescription: Excessive, persistent fear or worry that is out of proportion to any real threat — and impairs daily functioning.

entries.title: Bipolar Disorder
entries.contentDescription: A lifelong mood disorder defined by episodes of mania/hypomania alternating with depression — where a single manic episode is the diagnosis, not the depression.

entries.title: Schizophrenia
entries.contentDescription: A chronic psychotic disorder of dopamine dysregulation — where positive symptoms, negative symptoms, and cognitive decline converge to fracture reality testing.

entries.title: Alcohol & Substance Withdrawal
entries.contentDescription: Abrupt cessation of a chronically-used depressant unmasks a hyperexcitable, catecholamine-driven nervous system — a spectrum from tremor to life-threatening delirium tremens.

entries.title: Delirium
entries.contentDescription: An acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness caused by an underlying medical insult — it is a medical emergency, not a psychiatric diagnosis of exclusion.

entries.title: Suicide Risk Assessment
entries.contentDescription: Suicide risk is dynamic, not static — the goal is not to predict but to identify modifiable risk, ensure safety, and intervene before intent becomes action.

entries.title: Preeclampsia & Eclampsia
entries.contentDescription: New-onset hypertension with end-organ dysfunction after 20 weeks — a placenta-driven syndrome where the only cure is delivery.

entries.title: Gestational Diabetes
entries.contentDescription: Placental hormones drive maternal insulin resistance that outstrips pancreatic reserve — glucose intolerance first recognized in pregnancy.

entries.title: Postpartum Hemorrhage
entries.contentDescription: The leading cause of maternal death worldwide — most often a boggy, atonic uterus that won't clamp down after delivery.

entries.title: Labor & Delivery Stages
entries.contentDescription: Labor is the physiologic progression of regular, painful uterine contractions producing cervical change and fetal descent — organized into three (functionally four) stages that guide every intrapartum decision.

entries.title: Bronchiolitis (RSV)
entries.contentDescription: A viral lower-airway infection of infants — inflamed, mucus-clogged bronchioles cause the hallmark wheeze and crackles in babies under 2.

entries.title: Croup
entries.contentDescription: Viral swelling of the subglottic larynx and trachea — the toddler with a barking, seal-like cough and inspiratory stridor.

entries.title: Pressure Injuries
entries.contentDescription: Localized skin and soft-tissue damage over a bony prominence from sustained pressure and shear — a largely preventable injury that is a key marker of care quality.

entries.title: Burns
entries.contentDescription: Thermal, chemical, electrical, or radiation injury to tissue — where depth and body surface area drive fluid resuscitation, infection risk, and survival.

entries.title: Surgical Wound Care & Dehiscence
entries.contentDescription: A surgical incision that fails to heal and splits open — where recognizing serosanguineous drainage before frank separation prevents catastrophic evisceration.

entries.title: Anaphylaxis
entries.contentDescription: A rapid, IgE-driven multisystem allergic reaction — epinephrine is the only life-saving first-line drug, not antihistamines.

entries.title: Shock (Types & Management)
entries.contentDescription: Shock is a state of inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular oxygen delivery — a hemodynamic emergency where the diagnosis is the resuscitation.

entries.title: Acute Abdomen
entries.contentDescription: Sudden severe abdominal pain demanding rapid triage — the central question is always "does this belong to the surgeon?"

entries.title: Pediatric Fever & Sepsis Workup
entries.contentDescription: Fever in a child is common and usually benign — but the job of the workup is to catch the rare invasive bacterial infection and evolving septic shock before compensation fails.

entries.title: Hypernatremia
entries.contentDescription: A serum sodium >145 mEq/L that always signals a water deficit relative to sodium — a problem of too little free water, not too much salt.

entries.title: Hypokalemia
entries.contentDescription: Low serum potassium destabilizes membrane excitability — the heart and muscles pay the price first.

entries.title: Hypocalcemia
entries.contentDescription: Low serum calcium unmasks neuromuscular excitability — from tingling fingers to seizures and lethal laryngospasm.

entries.title: Hypercalcemia
entries.contentDescription: Too much calcium in the blood — bones, stones, groans, and psychiatric overtones from cellular hyperexcitability gone quiet.

entries.title: Hypomagnesemia
entries.contentDescription: The forgotten electrolyte — low magnesium destabilizes membranes, drags down potassium and calcium, and sets the stage for lethal arrhythmias.

entries.title: Phosphate Disorders
entries.contentDescription: Phosphate powers ATP and bone — too little starves cellular energy while too much precipitates with calcium and calcifies tissue.

entries.title: Metabolic Acidosis
entries.contentDescription: A primary fall in serum bicarbonate that drops blood pH — the body answers with rapid respiratory compensation while you hunt for the cause.

entries.title: Metabolic Alkalosis
entries.contentDescription: A primary rise in serum bicarbonate — sustained only when the kidney is stopped from excreting it, which is why the story splits into saline-responsive and saline-resistant disease.

entries.title: Respiratory Acidosis
entries.contentDescription: The lungs fail to blow off CO2 — alveolar hypoventilation raises PaCO2 and drops the blood pH.

entries.title: Respiratory Alkalosis
entries.contentDescription: Blowing off too much CO2 — alveolar hyperventilation drives up blood pH by lowering PaCO2.

entries.title: Hypovolemia / Fluid Volume Deficit
entries.contentDescription: A deficit of extracellular fluid volume — the body loses water and sodium together, shrinking circulating volume and threatening tissue perfusion.

entries.title: Fluid Volume Overload
entries.contentDescription: Too much salt and water in the wrong compartments — the body's tank overflows into lungs, veins, and tissues.

entries.title: Acetaminophen Overdose
entries.contentDescription: The most common cause of acute liver failure in the West — deadly precisely because early symptoms are silent while NAPQI quietly destroys the liver.

entries.title: Salicylate (Aspirin) Overdose
entries.contentDescription: A deceptively lethal acid-base puzzle — early respiratory alkalosis masks a lethal high anion-gap metabolic acidosis.

entries.title: Opioid Overdose
entries.contentDescription: A reversible respiratory emergency — opioids silence the brainstem's drive to breathe until naloxone or oxygen intervenes.

entries.title: Benzodiazepine Overdose
entries.contentDescription: GABA-A potentiation gone too far — CNS and respiratory depression that is usually survivable with airway support alone, where the antidote is often more dangerous than the poison.

entries.title: Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose
entries.contentDescription: A fast-moving toxidrome where sodium-channel blockade and anticholinergic effects converge — QRS widening and hypotension are the killers.

entries.title: Digoxin Toxicity
entries.contentDescription: A narrow-therapeutic-window cardiac glycoside gone rogue — digoxin immune Fab is the specific antidote that binds free drug and reverses life-threatening arrhythmias and hyperkalemia.

entries.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
entries.contentDescription: A colorless, odorless gas that binds hemoglobin ~200-250x tighter than oxygen — causing tissue hypoxia that pulse oximetry cannot see.

entries.title: Toxic Alcohols (Methanol/Ethylene Glycol)
entries.contentDescription: The parent alcohol is fairly benign — it's the toxic metabolites from alcohol dehydrogenase that blind, acidify, and destroy kidneys.

entries.title: Organophosphate Poisoning
entries.contentDescription: Irreversible acetylcholinesterase inhibition floods synapses with acetylcholine — producing a life-threatening cholinergic crisis reversed by atropine and pralidoxime.

entries.title: Breast Cancer
entries.contentDescription: Malignancy of breast ductal or lobular tissue whose treatment and prognosis hinge on stage and receptor status — ER, PR, and HER2.

entries.title: Colorectal Cancer
entries.contentDescription: The great masquerader of the gut — often silent until it bleeds, obstructs, or spreads, yet largely preventable through timely colonoscopy screening.

entries.title: Prostate Cancer
entries.contentDescription: The most common non-skin cancer in men — often indolent adenocarcinoma detected by PSA, but capable of lethal spread to bone.

entries.title: Pancreatic Cancer
entries.contentDescription: Painless jaundice in an older adult — the classic red flag for a pancreatic head adenocarcinoma obstructing the bile duct.

entries.title: Ovarian Cancer
entries.contentDescription: The silent killer — vague symptoms delay diagnosis until advanced-stage disease, making it the most lethal gynecologic malignancy.

entries.title: Cervical Cancer
entries.contentDescription: A largely preventable malignancy of the cervix driven by persistent high-risk HPV infection — caught early by screening, prevented by vaccination.

entries.title: Bladder Cancer
entries.contentDescription: Painless gross hematuria in an older smoker is bladder cancer until cystoscopy proves otherwise — never dismiss it as a UTI.

entries.title: Gastric Cancer
entries.contentDescription: A frequently silent adenocarcinoma of the stomach that presents late — vague dyspepsia masking H. pylori-driven malignancy until weight loss, obstruction, or metastasis appears.

entries.title: Melanoma
entries.contentDescription: A malignant tumor of melanocytes with high metastatic potential — early recognition and depth of invasion drive survival.

entries.title: Brain Tumors
entries.contentDescription: A fixed mass in a rigid skull — where even a benign tumor can kill by raising intracranial pressure.

entries.title: Tumor Lysis Syndrome
entries.contentDescription: Massive tumor cell death dumps intracellular contents into the blood — an oncologic emergency of hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and hypocalcemia.

entries.title: Febrile Neutropenia
entries.contentDescription: A single fever in a neutropenic host is a true oncologic emergency — empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour save lives, so treat first and investigate second.

entries.title: Malignant Spinal Cord Compression
entries.contentDescription: New or worsening back pain in a cancer patient is cord compression until proven otherwise — hours matter because function lost is rarely regained.

entries.title: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
entries.contentDescription: Obstruction of the superior vena cava chokes venous return from the head, neck, and arms — an oncologic emergency when it compromises the airway or brain.

entries.title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
entries.contentDescription: The most common endocrine disorder of reproductive-age women — a triad of ovulatory dysfunction, hyperandrogenism, and insulin resistance.

entries.title: Endometriosis
entries.contentDescription: Endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus — cyclic pelvic pain, infertility, and estrogen-driven inflammation in reproductive-age women.

entries.title: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
entries.contentDescription: Ascending infection of the upper female genital tract — treat empirically on minimal criteria because the cost of missing it is infertility.

entries.title: Ectopic Pregnancy
entries.contentDescription: A pregnancy implanted outside the uterine cavity — a leading cause of first-trimester maternal death when it ruptures.

entries.title: Ovarian Torsion
entries.contentDescription: Sudden severe unilateral pelvic pain in a woman with an adnexal mass — a time-sensitive surgical emergency to save the ovary.

entries.title: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding
entries.contentDescription: Bleeding that is abnormal in frequency, regularity, duration, or volume — the FIGO PALM-COEIN system sorts every cause into a structural or non-structural bucket.

entries.title: Uterine Fibroids (Leiomyoma)
entries.contentDescription: Benign estrogen- and progesterone-driven smooth-muscle tumors of the uterus — the most common cause of menorrhagia and pelvic bulk symptoms in reproductive-age women.

entries.title: Menopause
entries.contentDescription: The permanent cessation of menses from ovarian follicular depletion — confirmed after 12 months of amenorrhea, not by a single lab.

entries.title: Kawasaki Disease
entries.contentDescription: An acute self-limited medium-vessel vasculitis of young children whose real danger is silent coronary artery aneurysm — treat early to protect the heart.

entries.title: Epiglottitis
entries.contentDescription: Rapidly progressive infection of the supraglottic structures — a true airway emergency where the child looks toxic and the epiglottis can swell shut in hours.

entries.title: Acute Otitis Media
entries.contentDescription: A middle-ear infection behind an intact eardrum — the bulging, erythematous tympanic membrane is the diagnostic hallmark.

entries.title: Intussusception
entries.contentDescription: Telescoping of one bowel segment into another — the most common cause of intestinal obstruction in children 6 months to 3 years.

entries.title: Pyloric Stenosis
entries.contentDescription: Hypertrophy of the pyloric muscle creates a gastric outlet obstruction in young infants — the classic triad is non-bilious projectile vomiting, a palpable olive, and hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

entries.title: Febrile Seizure
entries.contentDescription: A benign, age-dependent seizure triggered by fever in an otherwise neurologically healthy young child — reassurance, not a lifelong epilepsy diagnosis.

entries.title: Congenital Heart Defects
entries.contentDescription: Structural malformations of the heart present at birth — the pivotal question is always cyanotic vs acyanotic and whether flow is ductal-dependent.

entries.title: Failure to Thrive
entries.contentDescription: Inadequate growth in early childhood — a sign, not a diagnosis, driven by too few calories in, too few absorbed, or too many burned.

entries.title: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
entries.contentDescription: A sudden blockage of aqueous outflow spikes intraocular pressure — a true ocular emergency threatening irreversible vision loss within hours.

entries.title: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
entries.contentDescription: A chronic, painless optic neuropathy with an open anterior chamber angle — the "silent thief of sight" that erodes peripheral vision before the patient ever notices.

entries.title: Conjunctivitis
entries.contentDescription: Inflammation of the conjunctiva — a red, weepy eye that is usually benign but occasionally the first sign of a vision-threatening emergency.

entries.title: Retinal Detachment
entries.contentDescription: Sudden flashes, a shower of floaters, and a rising curtain over vision — a time-critical separation of the neurosensory retina that threatens sight.

entries.title: Age-Related Macular Degeneration
entries.contentDescription: Progressive degeneration of the central retina (macula) — the leading cause of irreversible central vision loss in adults over 50.

entries.title: Cataracts
entries.contentDescription: Progressive opacification of the crystalline lens causing painless, gradual vision loss — corrected definitively by surgical lens replacement.

entries.title: Uveitis
entries.contentDescription: Inflammation of the uveal tract (iris, ciliary body, choroid) — a vision-threatening process that is frequently the eye's warning flare for a systemic autoimmune or infectious disease.

entries.title: Orbital Cellulitis
entries.contentDescription: A sight- and life-threatening infection posterior to the orbital septum — distinguished from benign preseptal cellulitis by proptosis, pain with eye movement, and ophthalmoplegia.

entries.title: Sinusitis (Rhinosinusitis)
entries.contentDescription: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses and nasal mucosa — overwhelmingly viral and self-limited, with antibiotics reserved for the minority that are truly bacterial.

entries.title: Streptococcal Pharyngitis
entries.contentDescription: Acute sore throat from group A Streptococcus — the one bacterial cause worth treating primarily to prevent acute rheumatic fever.

entries.title: Epistaxis
entries.contentDescription: Nosebleed — most bleeds are anterior from Kiesselbach's plexus and self-limited, but posterior bleeds can be brisk, airway-threatening emergencies.

entries.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
entries.contentDescription: Dislodged otoconia drifting through the semicircular canals — brief, positional spinning triggered by head movement.

entries.title: Otitis Externa
entries.contentDescription: Inflammation of the external auditory canal — the classic swimmer's ear driven by moisture, trauma, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

entries.title: Peritonsillar Abscess
entries.contentDescription: The most common deep neck space infection of adults — a collection of pus between the tonsillar capsule and pharyngeal muscles that pushes the uvula aside and muffles the voice.

entries.title: Meniere's Disease
entries.contentDescription: A disorder of the inner ear's fluid balance — recurrent spontaneous vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness.

entries.title: Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
entries.contentDescription: Reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus in a sensory ganglion — producing a painful, unilateral dermatomal vesicular rash.

entries.title: Psoriasis
entries.contentDescription: Immune-driven epidermal hyperproliferation — chronic, well-demarcated silvery-scaled plaques on extensor surfaces.

entries.title: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema)
entries.contentDescription: A chronic, relapsing, intensely pruritic inflammatory dermatosis of a defective skin barrier — the itch that rashes, not the rash that itches.

entries.title: Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer (BCC/SCC)
entries.contentDescription: Chronic UV damage to keratinocytes drives the two most common human cancers — basal cell carcinoma (locally destructive, rarely metastatic) and squamous cell carcinoma (can metastasize).

entries.title: Urticaria (Hives)
entries.contentDescription: Transient, intensely pruritic wheals from mast-cell histamine release — each individual lesion resolves within 24 hours without leaving a mark.

entries.title: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN
entries.contentDescription: A rare, life-threatening drug-induced mucocutaneous reaction — keratinocytes undergo widespread apoptosis, sheeting the skin off like a burn.

entries.title: Contact Dermatitis
entries.contentDescription: An eczematous skin reaction to an external agent — either direct chemical injury (irritant) or a delayed immune response (allergic).

entries.title: Acne Vulgaris
entries.contentDescription: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the pilosebaceous unit — where androgens, excess sebum, hyperkeratinization, and Cutibacterium acnes converge to produce comedones and inflammatory lesions.
